title: Read boundary, version 1
description: The manifest, the page envelope, the call-search row and the read-result wrapper. These are the shapes that cross the authorized read boundary; route spelling follows the host application's conventions and is not part of this contract.

manifest.title: The pointer to a subject's current revision
manifest.description:
Written **last**: the producer writes immutable details and the digest, validates them, and only then publishes the manifest atomically. That ordering is the whole concurrency story — a reader either sees the old generation or the new one, never a half-written one, and a failed reprocess leaves the previous usable revision in place.

The manifest is the only mutable object in the analytics tree. Everything it points at is immutable, which is what lets a reader pin a revision and page it safely while a new generation is being written beside it.

digestKey.description: Where the current revision's digest lives, relative to the analytics root. A storage key, resolved server-side: it is never handed to a browser and no client-supplied value is ever substituted for it.

supersedes.description: The revision this one replaced, where known. Retention of old revisions is a separate policy that must respect active readers.

page.title: One page of a detail or search resource
page.description:
`revision` is echoed so a reader can detect mid-read drift rather than discovering it as inconsistent numbers. `nextCursor: null` ends pagination — an empty `items` with a non-null cursor is legal and means 'keep asking', which is how a server that filters server-side avoids guessing a page size.

Cursors are opaque and bind tenant, filters and revision together. A cursor replayed against different filters or a newer revision is rejected explicitly, never silently reinterpreted.

pageLimits.description: Default and maximum page sizes, as data so both implementations agree. A server may return fewer than asked.

callSearchRow.title: One row of a call search result
callSearchRow.description: Deliberately thin: enough to rank, judge completeness and navigate, and nothing that would tempt a reader to compute with it. `digestRevision` pins what the row was derived from, so following it cannot land on figures from a newer generation than the row.

impairment.description: All-category union exposure, as a whole ImpairmentExposure rather than a bare share, so a reader always has the denominator and the unknown time beside the impaired time.

callSearchQuery.title: The supported call-search filters
callSearchQuery.description: Exactly the filters the contract names. The UI advertises which combinations are supported rather than offering every pairing and quietly dropping the ones the server cannot answer; combined cohort filters go through this query and are never inferred from marginal cohort totals.

missingDataOnly.description: The filter that makes calls excluded from the worst-call ranking — those with no assessed evidence — discoverable rather than invisible.

readResult.title: The outcome of an authorized read
readResult.description:
Six states, each needing its own UI treatment. `ready` with an empty digest is a verified empty period; `pending` is a job that has not produced one. A stale but usable revision stays `ready` and carries a freshness warning instead of being downgraded — withholding usable figures because they are an hour old helps nobody.

Offering retry on `failed` must not implicitly start processing: a read is a read.

staleness.description: Present when the served revision is usable but known to lag. Separate from `state` on purpose.

allOf.description: Every non-ready state must say why, in codes the label map can render.
An unsupported version reports the version it found, so the message can name it.
